core: type, class, ID, and attribute selectors
supporting: matching elements in a document tree

claims.claim: A CSS selector is a pattern used to select elements in a document tree for styling.
A type selector matches elements by their element name, while class and ID selectors use class and id attribute values.
An attribute selector can match an element based on whether it has an attribute or on an attribute value.
Whitespace between selectors is the descendant combinator and matches an element that has an ancestor matching the selector to its left.
A compound selector combines simple selectors with no combinator, so every component must match the same element.
